notes.title: Pondering My Orb
notes.content:
Thanks largely to player feedback, there have been updates to camera behavior, and traps have been made a bit more fair while still being quite deadly.  There have also been improvements to particle effects and game balance.

Also, special thanks goes out to Chris Doerksen for providing the music for level 2!  It really fits the vibe of the game perfectly ;)  Checkout more of his work on SoundCloud.com.


Music
 Awesome new song for level 2 from Chris Doerksen, "Chase." Ultra Paralax 2022.

Balance & Gameplay
 Altered the stone ball trap to make it more fair to the player and to allow for more emergent situations.
 Optimized AI spawning in Dungeon.
 Adjusted enemy spawn count.
 Axe and saw blade traps are no longer insta-kills to game characters, but instead do rapid damage that can quickly become lethal.
 Weapons in hand will now collide with wall and environment if too close.

Camera
 Changed aim camera offsets to improve the view when the player is aiming backed against a wall.
 Stopped weapon, ammo, money and potion pickups from interacting with the camera collider for a much smoother experience. 
 Fixed issue with camera FOV.

 Improved player death event by hiding HUD elements and disabling player ragdoll coliders post warp fx for a cleaner effect.
 Fixed issue with blood splatter fx and level loading, AI death function..
 Added more blood fx.

notes.title: Feeling good!
notes.content:
It has been an incredible launch week for Secrets of the Witch House and I am thrilled with the reception players and streamers have given the game so far.  It feels surreal to launch a game on Steam, and to get such a warm welcome has been amazing ;)

Also, as there is no rest for the wicked, this week also featured several game updates focusing on performance, the Dark Fortress level geometry and generation, as well as adjusting some of the AI enemy behaviors:

Thank you all for a wonderful launch week, and remember to leave a positive review if you are enjoying the game ;)

Best,
The Warden

notes.title: Secrets of the Witch House is LIVE!
notes.content:
Today is launch day and I am electrified with excitement to share Secrets of the Witch House with the world.  I want to thank everyone who made this day possible.  Gamers, family, friends, content creators, asset developers, and community members have all been integral to launching this game.  I could not have done it without you, and you have my eternal gratitude.

THANK YOU!

What's next for Secrets of the Witch House?  Initially the focus will be on addressing player feedback and any technical issues players may discover.  Moving forward the rough roadmap looks something like this:

 More rooms
 More enemies
 More traps
 More treasures
 More destruction
 More secrets
 And possibly even hats... ;)

Deeper and Deeper
I am thrilled to begin this journey with you, and I thank you for joining me. Together we will see just how deep this rabbit hole goes.  ;)

Sincerely,
The Warden

notes.title: What does it all mean?
notes.content:
There have been many updates in the last few weeks as the result watching game reviewers and creators play Secrets of the Witch House on social media, and I wanted to give some context to the patch notes I usually post.

No matter how much testing I do there is no substitute for watching a player in their own environment completely apart from the me, the developer.

Watching streams and videos I can only observe and absorb what is working and not working about the experience, what the player loves and dislikes, where they are confused or enthusiastic, and where they are having the most fun.  It is the best game feedback there is and it gets used to make a galaxy of improvements that each move the game miles forward.

After watching these play-throughs and considering improvements, each update published seeks to:

 Optimize controls and interfaces.  
 Adjust difficulty.
 Better communicate features.
 Address bugs.
 Improve enemy placement and combat flow.
 Improve camera features and control.
 Balance combat.
 Adjust the economy and reward systems.
 Adjust ammo/weapon pickups, frequency and quantity.
 Improve level designs.
 Improve AI pathing.
 Improve level generation.
And to just make more things go BOOM.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43666101/9073b39440db1889577a1c9af0bbb0fc369681ca.png
That's why we're here really.

Thank you to all the creators and reviewers that have been a part of this.  The game is better after each update because of your support and curiosity.

Sincerely,
The Warden
